newsitem.title: USA: Stryker sees lower Matsumoto Q4 sales.
newsitem.headline: Stryker sees lower Matsumoto Q4 sales.

text.p: Stryker Corp, which makes and markets specialty surgical and medical products, said it expects sales from its 51 percent Japanese distribution venture in the 1996 fourth quarter to be significantly lower than the same period in 1995.
Japan Matsumoto Medical Instruments Inc, a distributor of medical devices in Japan, is a 51 percent owned subisidiary of Stryker.

In a quarterly filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Stryker said the significant decline in sales of Matsumoto does not have as significant an effect on the Stryker's net earnings because distributed products generally have lower margins.
Stryker had reported 1996 third quarter earnings rose 20 percent from the same period a year ago to $24.2 million or $0.25 a share. Sales increased nine percent to $223.6 million.
Domestic sales were up 22 percent in the third quarter, while international sales fell eight percent, it had reported.

Lower sales in Japan more than offset strong shipments in other international markets. Sales in Japan declined 26 percent in the third quarter and 34 percent in the first nine months of the year because of lower Matsumoto shipments and unfavorable currency comparisons, the company had said.

Sales of Matsumoto fell 49 percent in the third quarter and 60 percent in the nine months, reflecting termination of several distribution arrangements and unfavorable foreign currency comparisons of the joint venture, Stryker had said.

In the filing, Stryker also said its financial position at September 30 remained strong with cash and marketable securities of $250.2 million and working capital of $453 million. The company generated $78.5 million in cash from operations in the first nine months of 1996 compared with $64.5 million in the same period of 1995.
